data_source: EEA Waterbase (WISE-6) Water Quality dataset, European Environment Agency
filtered_to: river monitoring stations, annual aggregates, 2010-2024, 6 EU countries
risk_label_method: rule-based, derived from cited regulatory/scientific freshwater-quality thresholds (Section 4): DO/BOD5/Ammonium/pH from EU Directive 2006/44/EC (repealed 2013, consolidated into WFD 2000/60/EC -- cited as literature reference values, not current binding law); Nitrate set at half the EU Nitrates Directive 91/676/EEC (still in force) 50 mg/L threshold; Total Phosphorus from cross-jurisdictionally corroborated eutrophication literature (US EPA 1986, CONAMA 357/2005). Full citations in notebook Section 4. Still a prototype screening rule, not a current official regulatory classification for any specific jurisdiction.

bangladesh_data.source: Bangladesh DoE River/Surface & Ground Water Quality Reports (2010-2023, government monthly monitoring) merged with the REACH-Dhaka field dataset (Univ. of Oxford REACH programme, 2017-2021); DoE Surface & Ground Water Quality Report 2016's own Chapter 6 trend table closes the earlier 2016 reporting gap for Buriganga/Turag/Shitalakhya and the Bangladesh Environment Conservation Rules, 2023 (Gazette, 5 Mar 2023) for regulatory thresholds
bangladesh_data.coverage: 40 rivers/canals, station-month granularity, 2010-2023 (own merged raw dataset)
bangladesh_data.observations: 36,316 raw rows -> powered evaluation uses 2,070 station-months across 28 rivers, 176 stations (2021-2023)
bangladesh_data.type: real government + university field measurements, never simulated -- see /api/master/summary and /api/bangladesh/doe_eval for the full breakdown
bangladesh_data.usage: independent external stress-testing and regulatory compliance-checking only -- never used to train the EU classifier
attribution: Bangladesh Department of Environment (DoE) -- River Water Quality Reports 2010/2013/2015/2016 and Surface & Ground Water Quality Reports 2021-2023. Used per DoE's own usage note: 'freely for study, research and training purposes subject to acknowledgement of the source.'

REACH: Improving water security for the poor, University of Oxford (UK-aid/FCDO funded) -- Greater Dhaka watershed water quality dataset, 58 sampling points, 2017-2021. Creators: Hossain, M.A., Shawal, S. et al. See reachwater.uk/datasets -- cite the dataset DOI directly, do not redistribute the raw workbook without checking its stated license.

Bangladesh Gazette, Additional Issue, 5 March 2023 -- Environment Conservation Rules 2023 (পরিবেশ সংরক্ষণ বিধিমালা, ২০২৩), Schedule-2. Threshold values transcribed from the gazette image; verify before citing as binding law.

single_point_sites.source: manually compiled from published field studies of the Buriganga and Turag rivers (Dhaka, Bangladesh)
single_point_sites.type: single-point-in-time field observations, not a downloadable raw dataset, not a time series

cross_region_result_summary.interpretation: The model systematically under-predicts risk severity for Bangladesh rivers, and its own out-of-distribution flag is a strong (AUROC 0.895), usable warning sign for exactly the cases where it is wrong -- across both the smaller 3-river annual panel and the larger 28-river, station-month powered evaluation.
